subject.title: fix(browser): retire durable tab rows whose browser never returns

question: Should durable browser-tab ownership be abandoned after 24 hours of failed browser identity lookup, accepting that a browser which later returns may keep an unmanaged tab?
rationale: The change is a deliberate persistent-cleanup policy boundary, not only an implementation detail: it exchanges indefinite retry and possible registry exhaustion for eventual loss of later cleanup capability.

options.title: Accept bounded retirement
options.body: Adopt the unavailable-only 24-hour retirement rule after adding real-browser proof that it recovers the durable-store capacity failure.

options.title: Keep indefinite ownership retry
options.body: Preserve current retry semantics and pursue a different capacity-management or operator-recovery design without deleting unavailable ownership records.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded retirement
recommendation.body: Adopt the unavailable-only 24-hour retirement rule after adding real-browser proof that it recovers the durable-store capacity failure.

likelyOwner.reason: FMLS introduced the merged durable browser-tab ownership and restart-cleanup model that defines the tradeoff this follow-up changes.
